status: Computational hypotheses; not measured subjective experience

aptenodytes-forsteri.method: For an ideal diamond, area = width × height / 2. Relative area is the product of the two diagonal ratios. Scale linear RGB by that product as an exposure illustration; no diamond-shaped field mask is imposed.
aptenodytes-forsteri.evidence: Strongly constricted emperor-penguin pupils were diamond shaped in a comparative optical study.
aptenodytes-forsteri.limits: Assigned dimensions, fixed irradiance and no adaptation. Pupil shape does not make the scene diamond-shaped. No fitted color perception, underwater optics or low-light threshold.
aptenodytes-forsteri.validation: Fit species-specific pupil geometry and irradiance measurements; validate separately in air and water.
aptenodytes-forsteri.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

rhincodon-typus.method: Calculate an A1 alpha-band template at nominal peak 478 nm. Keep the photograph unchanged: RGB cannot determine per-pixel spectra or receptor catches.
rhincodon-typus.evidence: Reconstituted whale-shark rhodopsin peaks at 478 nm; molecular experiments link substitutions to spectral tuning and stability.
rhincodon-typus.limits: In-vitro peak is not a color percept. No fitted thermal kinetics, pigment concentration, cone signal, depth or water attenuation.
rhincodon-typus.validation: Measure ocular transmission and calibrated spectral scenes; test predictions with independent live-animal responses.
rhincodon-typus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

carcharodon-carcharias.method: Interpolate linear RGB toward human-weighted luminance. Default removes chromatic cues as a hypothesis, not a measured white-shark transfer function.
carcharodon-carcharias.evidence: Retinal opsin evidence supports cone monochromacy in lamniform sharks, including white shark.
carcharodon-carcharias.limits: Rod–cone interactions, adaptation, motion and neural weighting are omitted. Grayscale is a display convention, not proof of subjective black-and-white experience.
carcharodon-carcharias.validation: Use retinal spectra and intensity-controlled discrimination trials; validate recognition independently.
carcharodon-carcharias.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

ocypode-quadrata.method: Keep an assigned central disk detailed; pool linear RGB outside it. The disk is an explanatory mask, not a fitted map of individual ommatidia.
ocypode-quadrata.evidence: Ghost-crab eye morphology shows an anterior acute zone; ERG experiments found a single 494 nm sensitivity peak.
ocypode-quadrata.limits: ERG peak is not a complete color transform. Radius, center and pooling are assumptions; no panoramic field, acceptance angles or detection thresholds are reconstructed.
ocypode-quadrata.validation: Fit eye geometry and receptor fields, then test independent target-detection tasks.
ocypode-quadrata.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

palaemon-serratus.method: For hypothetical orthogonal ideal analyzers, I0 = (1 + p cos 2θ)/2 and I90 = (1 − p cos 2θ)/2. Calculate their difference. Keep habitat RGB unchanged.
palaemon-serratus.evidence: Pooled Palaemon shrimp responded to intensity gratings but not polarization-only gratings in a gaze-stabilization assay.
palaemon-serratus.limits: Phone RGB does not measure polarization. Analyzer channels are physics inputs, not fitted prawn receptors or predicted gaze; negative assay results do not exclude other polarization tasks.
palaemon-serratus.validation: Use species-separated trials, matched intensity and measured Stokes inputs; test behavior independently.
palaemon-serratus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

osphranter-rufus.method: Remove a chosen fraction of linear-RGB chromatic differences. This deliberately tests information loss without inventing measured kangaroo cone peaks.
osphranter-rufus.evidence: A marsupial genome comparison includes red kangaroo and proposes Macropus-lineage visual adaptations from sequence changes.
osphranter-rufus.limits: Genomic inference is not a behavioral color test. This is neither a dichromat simulator nor a calibrated kangaroo percept; UV and twilight performance remain unmeasured.
osphranter-rufus.validation: Establish pigment spectra, ocular transmission and brightness-controlled behavior in this species.
osphranter-rufus.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

asterias-rubens.method: Average luminance in user-selected vertical sectors. Five is an illustrative starting value, not one camera sector per arm or a measured retinal sampling count.
asterias-rubens.evidence: Opsin studies distinguish optic cushions from putative extraocular photosensory tissue in Asterias rubens.
asterias-rubens.limits: No stitched five-eye percept, spectral sensitivity or acuity is fitted. Body orientation and extraocular sensing are omitted; this is an information diagram.
asterias-rubens.validation: Measure each eye’s field and response, then test directional behavior independently.
asterias-rubens.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

hydra-vulgaris.method: Illustrative gate = 1/(1 + coefficient × illumination). The uniform display shows the assigned gate, not a camera picture or fitted firing probability.
hydra-vulgaris.evidence: Bright light reduced stinging-cell discharge in experiments published as H. magnipapillata, now H. vulgaris.
hydra-vulgaris.limits: Equation is an authored hypothesis; no estimated coefficients, receptor activation or firing rates. Mechanical and chemical cues and strain variation are omitted.
hydra-vulgaris.validation: Fit trial-level light/mechanical/chemical experiments, then test a held-out strain and exposure range.
hydra-vulgaris.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

lymnaea-stagnalis.method: Compute max(0, earlier − later) and a relative decrease when earlier is nonzero. Display the absolute decrease as a uniform signal; no flicker is emitted.
lymnaea-stagnalis.evidence: Mantle photoreceptors participate in light-off responses connected to withdrawal. Lymnaea also has eyes; this study isolates the dermal pathway.
lymnaea-stagnalis.limits: Levels are supplied assumptions, not calibrated camera irradiance. No neural delay, habituation or withdrawal probability is fitted; not a reconstruction of ocular vision.
lymnaea-stagnalis.validation: Fit irradiance-step recordings with individual and adaptation effects; test independent time series.
lymnaea-stagnalis.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

lumbricus-terrestris.method: Compute lux × hours as a descriptive exposure integral. A uniform field shows assigned lux normalized to the control range; it is not the worm’s brightness experience.
lumbricus-terrestris.evidence: A 2025 experiment found reduced nighttime foraging at 10 lx and above under controlled-room conditions; field outcomes differed.
lumbricus-terrestris.limits: Lux weights human photopic sensitivity. No camera lux measurement, biological threshold, reciprocity law or behavioral dose-response is assumed. Spectrum, moisture, duration and context matter.
lumbricus-terrestris.validation: Use measured spectral irradiance, exposure history and independent behavioral datasets; compare field and laboratory settings.
lumbricus-terrestris.uncertainty: Scenario controls are not confidence intervals. No fitted perceptual dataset or independent validation.

softwareValidation: See repository checks and release evidence; unit tests do not validate animal perception.
